key_insight: Prediction errors followed power-law decreases as training datasets grew, despite non-ideal experimental variability in radiative-cooling coatings.
engineering_relevance: Learning curves can help estimate the value of additional experiments, while inverse models propose coating designs that can be screened for fabrication ease, cost, and scalability.
method: Automate fabrication and optical characterization across nine material and processing parameters.
Train forward and inverse neural networks and a spectrum-conditioned diffusion model on 10–10,000 samples.
Experimentally validate inverse designs against a broadband-emitter target.
evidence_signal: The platform produced 11,520 coatings; all model types exhibited power-law error scaling, and larger training datasets yielded experimentally validated spectra closer to the target.
watch_item: Scaling demonstrated for this coating platform may not transfer to other material systems or fabrication conditions without validation.
paper_title: Scaling laws in machine learning on non-ideal experimental data enable inverse design of radiative-cooling coatings
